criteria.note: The new assertion at :428-433 holds the isAbsolute guard (security-probe-plan.mjs:178) with an absolute name that resolves inside the directory. The earlier test at :95 covers an absolute outside name, a '../' name and a symlink. Run here, the test file passes 10 of 10.

criteria.description: No new test case over 1s; five runs, slowest per run with /proc/loadavg beside each, on PR head
criteria.note: Bound: no case over 1 s. The qa.3 Addendum records five runs of 'TMPDIR=/tmp CI=true command node --test --test-reporter=spec' on the two new test files, each with /proc/loadavg beside it. The slowest cases were 374.7, 384.9, 381.4, 357.7 and 410.7 ms, a median of 381.4 ms and a maximum of 410.7 ms. I re-ran the third test file here: 388.7 ms for the slowest case. Code at bd986dc0 is the same as at PR head e8a9f4d6, because only task documents were added after the one test assertion. Runs 1 to 4 show an identical load triple, which is a weakness in the record. The margin of more than 2x makes it immaterial.

criteria.description: bundle --check reports 0 problems; CI=true npm test passes
criteria.note: I ran 'npm run bundle -- --check' here: 129 skills, 0 problems. qa.4 records ci:fast exit 0 and 41 of 41 passing on the three related test files. The changed test file passes 10 of 10 here. .github/workflows/test.yml:58 runs npm test per PR. Since the prior judgement only a test file and task documents changed, and neither is bundled.

I ran 'python skills/create-skill/scripts/quick_validate.py skills/finalise' on HEAD: it passed and printed '✓ finalise'. qa.1:135 records the same run, and qa.2:71 records 'npm run validate -- skills/finalise/ # pass'. The criterion is a command outcome, not a behaviour a test can pin. Whether validate.yml runs it per PR was not checked.

criteria.note: The inline-cases branch still writes JSON.stringify(entryCases) (:466). The pre-existing Step 3b.1 fixtures at read-only-agent-writes.test.mjs:156, :211 and :264 run inline-cases plans. advisories.note: qa.3 Addendum timing runs 1 to 4 show an identical /proc/loadavg triple (2.22 3.82 3.99). The loads were probably sampled once per batch, not per run. It does not change the verdict, since the maximum is 410.7 ms against a 1000 ms bound.
Carried advisory: the test's 'seven' characters are U+0085, U+2028, U+2029, VT, FF, U+001F and CR, which is correct.
Carried advisory: the criterion says 'CI=true command npm test', and 'command' after an env assignment is not found in some shells, so the equivalent 'CI=true npm test' was used.
